description.narrative:
1. Objective of the project: Engage South East Asian countries in their energy transition to strengthen human rights and community-initiated renewable energy solutions.
2. Outcomes: Oxfam Indonesia commits to contribute to the two outcomes of I-JET below:
Outcome 1: Non-state actors at the national and regional level activity contribute to shifting the narrative toward a gender-responsive and socially inclusive energy transition Indicators for reporting could be but not be limited to: (1) Evidence of strengthened capacity/achieving capacity development plan milestones (2) Number of non-state actors regularly engaging in network meetings/events (3) Network participants demonstrate meetings and events build the capacity and influence of non stateactors (4) Evidence of increased CSO capacity (5) Number of initiatives that advocate for just and fair transitions that are socially and gender inclusive. (6) Evidence of strengthened capacity and connection of local networks and organizations to influence national/international platforms in decision making (7) Number of collaborative learning pieces
Outcome 2: National and regional level energy policy frameworks and financing mechanisms are gender-responsive and be socially inclusive.
Indicators for reporting could be but not be limited to: (1) Evidence of changes to policies and processes that increase low-carbon actions that are fair and gender-responsive (2) # of events with women meaningfully participating/leading (3) The extent to which partners integrate gender mainstreaming as seen in partner profiles (4) % increase of invitations to attend/participate in local, national and regional events/forums etc
3. Outputs: for 2023-2024, Oxfam in Indonesia through I-JET Indonesiaproject will produce the following outputs:
• A regional convening on JET will be organized to define a position and statement of CSOs before the ASEAN summit in Indonesia. • CSOs are informed about the commitment of ASEAN on JET. • CSOs and WROs will dialogue with relevant ASEAN platforms to strengthen their mutual relationship and understanding. • CSOs and WROs network will be strengthened to promote feminist principles and gender responsiveness into JET in Indonesia and the region. • Attend ASEAN or related events at the regional level • Participate in training and decimate the concept and principles of I-JET to stakeholders
4. Roles and responsibilities of Oxfam in Indonesia
- Develop an understanding of the baseline to deliver the intended outcomes and outputs. - Update and share the context and stakeholders of I-JET in Indonesia and ASEAN with regional meetings of I-JET project. - Implement the I-JET Indonesia project to deliver outputs and outcomes as stated above. - Share progress andachievement of building an alliance between CSOs and WROs to advance feminist principles and gender responsiveness into JET in Indonesia and the region - Develop relationship and collaboration and synergy building with NGOs that are members of I-JET project-funded regional partners (eg. Hivos of CANSEA). - Participate in J-JET relevant governance (coordination group meeting; and steering group meeting) meetings and in any regional events that are initiated by I-JET PMU - Share knowledge and lessons learned with the I-JET project in national and regional events. - Conduct assessment to ensure compliance on safeguarding. - Ensure and report that vulnerable groups including youth, women and indigenous peoples and their agencies are included inthe dialogue process. - Develop and submit both narrative and financial reports on time following AUS/ANCP reporting formats. - Provide quarterly updates on the delivery status of the project budget.

participating-org.narrative:
We have a vision of an Indonesia where people live equitably and free from the injustice of poverty, enjoy their rights, and are resilient in times of disasters. Women and girls are at the heart of all our strategies to achieve this vision.
We have been working with local and national partners in Indonesia since 1957.
We are currently working in 7 provinces where we are support the Government of Indonesia, civil society, and local communities on the following main issues:
Gender justice: We workwith women and girls to control their body and resources, and to participate equally in all economic, social, political and cultural aspects of their lives,to have leadership roles, access to resources and services and participate in decisions that affect their lives.
Economic justice:We work through partners with marginalized small holder farmers, especially women, to adapt to climate change and improve their food security. We promote inclusive natural resource management and to promote private sector accountability which encourages respect for women-led small holders and worker’s rights.
Climate Justice and Rights in crisis: we work with communies particulalry women to be more resilience towards climate change and disaster, including in climatefinancing and mitigation that one of focus is promoting gender just energy transition. We promote risk management as everybody’s business, to strengthen and mobilize the capacity of urban areas to respond to natural disasters. We promote the mainstreaming of gender in all response intervention conducted by national andsub-national governments.
